answer: Nonce-Ledger Entry: each identity must submit a fresh solution to a time-locked puzzle whose difficulty is set per submission and whose accepted answers are permanently retired. The ledger forces any new identity to wander through unsolved space, and the puzzle horizon resets after each accepted entry, so copies fail verification. An attacker who wants N identities pays N sequential compute costs, and a gale of parallel submissions still waits on the same retiring queue, making mass creation linearly expensive rather than free.
